answer.decision: Adopt the managed search service behind an internal abstraction and portable index pipeline.
answer.action: Use the managed service for launch; define a vendor-neutral canonical search document, isolate provider-specific APIs behind an internal interface, automate reproducible indexing and bulk export, and test reindexing into an alternative engine before launch.
reasons: The managed service supplies faceting, typo tolerance, and near-real-time indexing, satisfying the required launch capabilities.
It offers the most credible path to the four-month deadline while the backend team is already at capacity.

Building immediately presents excessive delivery and operational risk: the prior six-engineer-week prototype achieved only basic keyword search, and cluster operation would require on-call ownership and recurring upgrades.
Delaying for dedicated hires would impose material commercial cost by forfeiting the contracted design-partner expansion.
Projected year-one cost is limited to 7 percent of the product infrastructure budget.
A canonical document format, internal interface, reproducible indexing, bulk export, and tested reindexing path materially reduce vendor lock-in.
assumptions: The managed service meets required indexing latency, scale, availability, security, and compliance needs under expected workloads.
The four-month schedule can accommodate the portability layer and a scoped migration-path test without jeopardizing launch.
The cost estimate includes relevant support, transfer, storage, and overage charges.
A practical migration path means tested data and indexing portability, while accepting that some relevance tuning and provider-specific behavior may require adaptation.
risks: Provider-specific ranking, query syntax, analytics, and tuning may leak through the abstraction and increase migration effort.
Usage growth or omitted charges could make managed-service costs materially higher than projected.
Bulk export does not by itself ensure a viable migration; schema compatibility, reindex duration, relevance parity, and cutover procedures require validation.
Vendor outages, quotas, regional limitations, or contract changes could affect reliability or economics.
Overgeneralizing the abstraction could slow launch, so it should cover core capabilities and explicitly contain optional provider-specific extensions.

citations.claim: The managed service supports all required launch features and provides a documented bulk export API.
The internal prototype required six engineer-weeks but delivered only basic keyword search without typo tolerance or faceting.
Operating the open-source cluster would require a rotating primary on-call owner and quarterly upgrade work.
A six-month delay would forgo a contracted design-partner expansion.
Projected year-one managed-service spend is 7 percent of the product infrastructure budget.
The data model can produce a vendor-neutral canonical search document before indexing.
Launch is required within four months, on-call headcount cannot increase this year, and the design must preserve a practical vendor migration path.
